entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 16_Psyche_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 3234 vertices and 6464 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 223 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (35°, -9°), period 4.195948 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 110.63570427797241 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/16Psyche/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 16_Psyche_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 16 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read longitude-first. Disc interior 673 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.15 (median) against a mirror margin of 1.06; 1 of 16 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. The lens stands on the silhouette registration recorded in the entry above and on the route proven against the Dawn mosaic on Vesta; this test adds no independent check for this body.

entries.subject: Cambioni et al. (2022) ALMA thermal-inertia and dielectric-constant maps
entries.finding: The Zenodo release (doi:10.5281/zenodo.6321315, CC BY 4.0) gives both properties per 5-degree node, 73 x 37, fitted to ALMA 1.3 mm images of 2019 June 19 at about 30 km resolution; 1,895 of 2,701 nodes are mapped. They ship as the Thermal inertia and Dielectric constant lenses on the ADAM mesh, one colour per node, with dropped nodes as the missing-data grid. Median uncertainties are 134 for thermal inertia and 1.9 for the dielectric constant.

entries.subject: Placing maps from the Shepard et al. (2021) body frame on the ADAM mesh
entries.finding: Mesh directions are carried into the map frame through Cambioni et al. (2022) equation 2 (TDB) and the LAM parameter file (UTC) at the ALMA midpoint. The map frame's state reproduces all 22 sub-observer longitudes of de Kleer et al. (2021) Table 1 to a mean of 0.04 deg and scatter 0.33 deg (1.68 deg if read in UTC). By shape alone, the release altitude map against the ADAM mesh peaks 1 deg from the placement at correlation 0.821; mirrored longitude peaks at 0.455, flipped latitude at 0.485, both at 0.618.

entries.subject: Longitudes 60 to 120 degrees west flagged by the authors
entries.finding: Cambioni et al. (2022) hatch this band because it was seen at high emission angles in under a third of the ALMA images and may contain unmapped topography. The nodes are drawn like the rest and the lens notes name the band; no separate mask is published.
entries.revisitWhen: A release masks or revises the band, or new thermal observations cover it at lower emission angles.

entries.subject: Time scale of the LAM spin parameter file
entries.finding: The file does not state UTC or TDB. It is read in UTC, as for the SPHERE photograph lens; a TDB reading moves the mesh prime meridian 1.65 deg in map longitude. The shape-only registration peaks 1 deg from the UTC placement and 3 deg from the TDB one, at correlations 0.821 and 0.822, too flat to decide on a 5-degree grid.
entries.revisitWhen: LAM or Vernazza et al. state the time scale of the phase epoch.

entries.subject: The release's brightness-temperature, residual and uncertainty maps
entries.finding: The time-averaged brightness temperature depends on the 2019 viewing and illumination geometry rather than a surface property, and the residual and goodness-of-fit maps describe the fit. The uncertainty maps are summarised in the README instead of drawn as lenses.
entries.revisitWhen: The app gains a way to show a map's uncertainty alongside its values.
